official.tuition_coverage_note: UIC's Scholarships page states the Admissions Scholarship type is 'full tuition for 4 years'. For the 2026 academic year the International Students Track tuition is 8,202,000 KRW per semester (8,416,000 KRW for the first semester), which is the amount waived; miscellaneous student fees of 56,000 KRW (61,000 KRW in the first semester) are charged on top and are not part of the waiver.
benefits: Full tuition for 4 years (International Students Track: 8,202,000 KRW per semester in 2026; 8,416,000 KRW for the first semester)
Automatic consideration - international students applying to UIC are considered as scholarship candidates with no separate scholarship application
Scholarship offer letter physically enclosed in the admission packet and sent to recipients individually
eligibility: Qualification: newly-admitted international students to UIC

Must hold or expect to hold a high school diploma or certificate of high school equivalency (Article 98 of the Enforcement Decree of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act) before matriculating; GED, home schooling, cyber schooling or equivalent certificates are not accepted

Must be a non-Korean with non-Korean parents under Article 3 of the Nationality Act; if the applicant or any parent has Korean dual citizenship the applicant is NOT eligible for the International Students Track

Ethnically Korean foreigners must hold legal documentation verifying renunciation of Korean citizenship, with foreign citizenship acquired before the applicant entered high school (before Grade 1 for adoptees)
Recipients must maintain a certain level of GPA each semester to stay eligible for the scholarship in the following semester
requirements: From the AY 2027 intake onward: documents proving English proficiency are REQUIRED (previously optional)

English proficiency may be proven by TOEFL PBT/CBT/iBT, IELTS, CEFR English Certification, IB DP English A: Language and Literature or Literature, or AP English Language and Composition / English Literature and Composition - no minimum scores apply; or a high school diploma from a school in a country where English is the sole official language (US, Canada excluding Quebec, UK, Australia, New Zealand); or a Medium of Instruction certificate for an entirely English-taught high school curriculum

High school transcripts and graduation (or expected graduation) certificates from overseas schools must carry Apostille stamps or Korean Embassy/Consulate authentication; documents in other languages need notarised English translations
Application fee of KRW 150,000 (direct application) or USD 150 (Common Application); UIC does not offer or accept a fee waiver
documents: Printed copy of the online application form (from the UIC online application or Common App)
Letter of Consent & Verification (downloadable from the UIC website)
Official transcripts from all high schools attended, with Apostille / Korean Consulate authentication
Certificate of graduation or expected graduation, with Apostille / Korean Consulate authentication
English proficiency test scores or accepted equivalents (no minimum scores)
One copy each of the applicant's and parents' passports or ID cards
One notarised copy of the applicant's birth certificate or notarised documentation verifying the parent relationship
Receipt of application fee payment (KRW 150,000 / USD 150)

For Chinese nationals: notarised copies of kinship certificate and household register; foreigners residing in Korea: parents' and applicant's Certification of Alien Registration; ethnically Korean foreigners: legal documentation of renunciation of Korean citizenship
selection_criteria: Document review scored out of 200 points - holistic review of academic achievements and non-academic accomplishments
Admission and scholarship decision on a combined total of 300 points; scholarship recipients are selected from admitted applicants according to their academic credentials
coverage: 8,202,000 KRW per semester on the International Students Track (2026 academic year; 8,416,000 KRW first semester)
Does not cover miscellaneous student fees (56,000 KRW per semester), personal expenses or living costs
application_method: Step 1 - Online application: apply through the UIC online application site or the Common Application, then print the registered information

Step 2 - Offline submission: post all hard-copy application materials so they physically arrive at the UIC International Admissions office (Daewoo Annex Hall #301, 50 Yonsei-ro, Seodaemun-gu, Seoul 03722) by the document submission deadline
Participate in the applicant-verification call and the assigned online interview slot
Scholarship offer arrives enclosed in the admission packet - no separate scholarship application exists
official.application_route: Apply online to UIC (direct online application or Common App) and post the hard-copy documents; scholarship consideration is automatic from the admission application.
official.citizenship_residency: Non-Korean applicant with non-Korean parents (Article 3 of the Nationality Act); any Korean dual citizenship of the applicant or a parent rules out the International Students Track; ethnically Korean foreigners need proof of renunciation of Korean citizenship
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the International Students Track and the Admissions Scholarship are for international applicants only; Korean nationals and dual citizens are not eligible for the track
official.description: UIC awards its Admissions Scholarship - full tuition for four years - to newly admitted international students, who are automatically considered as scholarship candidates during admission and selected from admitted applicants according to academic credentials. Recipients are notified individually with the offer enclosed in the admission packet and must maintain a certain level of GPA each semester to keep the award.
official.program_type: Undergraduate admissions scholarship with automatic consideration (full tuition, 4 years)
official.english_requirement: Required from the AY 2027 intake: TOEFL PBT/CBT/iBT, IELTS, CEFR English Certification, IB DP English A (Language and Literature or Literature), or AP English Language and Composition / Literature - all with no minimum scores; OR a high school diploma from a school in an English-only official-language country (US, Canada excluding Quebec, UK, Australia, New Zealand); OR a Medium of Instruction certificate for an all-English high school curriculum (substitutable via the Letter of Consent & Verification form)

not_confirmed: The specific GPA threshold needed to retain the award each semester (published only as 'a certain level of GPA')
Exact dates for the 2nd Round (Fall 2027 entry) - published as 'March, 2027' and labelled TBD
Number of scholarship recipients / award selection quotas
verification.notes: Tuition table (8,202,000 KRW International Students Track, 2026), scholarship terms, full application schedule, required documents and English rules were read directly from UIC's own Tuition fee & Scholarship and First Year Students (International) pages.

applicant_utility.summary: UIC's Admissions Scholarship wipes out tuition for all four years (8,202,000 KRW per semester on the 2026 figures), but you win it through admission itself - there is no separate scholarship form, so your transcript quality is the application. Two traps dominate: from the 2027 intake English proof is mandatory even though no minimum score applies, and hard-copy documents must physically land at the Seoul office by 17:00 on the deadline day, which UIC says it will never extend. Budget for the uncovered pieces - miscellaneous fees of about 56,000-61,000 KRW per semester plus Seoul living costs - because the waiver covers tuition only.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-Korean high-school leavers with non-Korean parents who want an English-medium liberal-arts and science degree and can self-fund roughly KRW 8-9 million per year in living expenses.
application_readiness_checklist: Book a TOEFL/IELTS/CEFR test now, or secure a Medium of Instruction certificate - English proof is compulsory from the 2027 intake but carries no minimum score
Start Apostille or Korean consulate authentication of transcripts and graduation certificates early; apostilled papers can follow later, but only by the designated post-acceptance date
Use a courier with a guaranteed delivery date so documents arrive before 17:00 KST on the document deadline - arrival, not postmark, counts
Complete the online application (direct or Common App) and print the registered form exactly as submitted
Diarise the verification call and online interview (11-12 Dec 2026 for 1st Round) and keep the email address on the application monitored
Pay the KRW 150,000 / USD 150 fee - there is no waiver - and keep the receipt
Plan to keep a solid GPA from semester one; the award is re-checked every semester
common_rejection_risks: Missing even one required document by the deadline means disqualification - no interview
Any Korean dual citizenship for the applicant or a parent voids the International Students Track
GED, home schooling or cyber schooling credentials do not satisfy the high school diploma requirement
Un-apostilled or non-English transcripts without notarised translations
Missing the pre-interview check-up call or the assigned interview slot
Name mismatches between passport, birth certificate and application form
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Application fee (KRW 150,000 / USD 150), miscellaneous student fees (56,000 KRW per semester, 61,000 KRW first semester), personal and living expenses in Seoul (the fee page states the total cost does not include personal expenses), plus apostille, notarisation, translation and international courier costs.
document_audit: Every applicant now needs English proof - a diploma from an English-speaking country or an MOI certificate counts, and the registrar can certify via UIC's Letter of Consent & Verification if an MOI letter is unobtainable
Chinese nationals additionally need notarised kinship and household-register copies; foreigners living in Korea need Alien Registration certificates for both applicant and parents
Originals are required unless a sealed or notarised copy replaces them, and nothing you submit is returned
If you report test scores directly (ETS code 9893, College Board 7441, Duolingo), you must also email uicadm@yonsei.ac.kr with your English name and test date and post a hard copy
Passports, birth certificate and parent-relationship documents must be notarised copies
alerts: The 2nd Round (Fall 2027 entry) is only published as 'March, 2027' and flagged TBD - watch UIC's Announcements page from February
UIC explicitly refuses deadline extensions under any circumstances
The scholarship follows admission: without an admission offer there is no award, and awards are limited to admitted applicants by academic credentials
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online (direct site or Common App), post the full paper packet to the UIC office, sit the online interview, then receive the scholarship offer inside the admission packet.

official.deadline_note: No application deadline is published. The Foreigner Special Scholarship page defines eligibility by enrolment status - full-time international students already enrolled in regular semesters through the international student admission track - and support is granted per regular semester rather than through an application window.
official.status_note: The Graduate School lists the Yonsei International Companion Scholarship as an ongoing Foreigner Special Scholarship type assessed per regular semester of enrolment; no application round, opening announcement or closing date is published.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The award is a fixed cash amount per regular semester (KRW 2,000,000 for master's, KRW 3,000,000 for doctoral, KRW 2,000,000 for integrated programmes); the page does not state that tuition is paid or waived.
benefits: Integrated master's and PhD programme: KRW 2,000,000 per semester
Paid per regular semester of enrolment for the duration of the supported semesters
eligibility: Full-time international students enrolled in regular semesters through the international student admission track at the Graduate School
Ineligible: students receiving full tuition scholarships (from Graduate School) for regular semesters
Ineligible: students in the College of Medicine, College of Dentistry, or College of Nursing
Ineligible: Graduate School students at Mirae Campus
requirements: Enrolment must be in a regular semester (extra or non-regular semesters are outside the award's scope)
To be paid, students must register a bank account in their own name on the Yonsei academic portal system
coverage: Master's programme: KRW 2,000,000 per regular semester
Doctoral programme: KRW 3,000,000 per regular semester
Integrated master's and PhD programme: KRW 2,000,000 per regular semester
Regular semesters only - 4 semesters for master's and PhD programmes, 6 semesters for the integrated programme
official.application_route: No separate scholarship application route is published on the Graduate School's Foreigner Special Scholarship page; eligibility follows enrolment in regular semesters through the international student admission track, and payment requires a bank account registered on the Yonsei portal.
official.citizenship_residency: International students admitted through the Graduate School's international student admission track
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the award is defined for full-time international students
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Not available to students in the College of Medicine, College of Dentistry or College of Nursing, students in contract-based programmes, or Graduate School students at Mirae Campus
official.duration: Regular semesters: 4 semesters for master's and PhD programmes, 6 semesters for the integrated master's and PhD programme
official.description: The Graduate School lists the Yonsei International Companion Scholarship among its Foreigner Special Scholarships for full-time international students enrolled in regular semesters through the international student admission track, paying a fixed per-semester amount - KRW 2,000,000 for master's and integrated students and KRW 3,000,000 for doctoral students - across the programme's regular semesters.
official.program_type: Graduate School foreigner special scholarship (per-semester stipend, no separate application)

not_confirmed: Whether the stipend covers living costs or travel - the page publishes only the fixed per-semester amounts
Whether the award is fully automatic or requires departmental nomination - no scholarship application procedure is published
Any English-proficiency condition attached to the scholarship itself
Application-window or renewal dates - support is defined per regular semester of enrolment
verification.notes: Per-semester amounts, eligibility, exclusions and duration were read from the Graduate School's Foreigner Special Scholarship table; disbursement rules (portal bank-account registration, repayment on leave or withdrawal) from its Scholarship application and payment page; international-track admission timing from the Spring 2027 Int'l Student Track page.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a per-semester stipend, not a fee waiver: KRW 2,000,000 for master's students, KRW 3,000,000 for doctoral students and KRW 2,000,000 for the integrated programme, paid only for regular semesters (four for master's and PhD, six for integrated). It stacks on top of admission rather than replacing tuition funding, so treat it as a living-cost top-up of roughly KRW 8 million across a standard master's. You do not apply separately - you qualify by being a full-time international-track student in a regular semester, but you must hold a bank account in your own name on the Yonsei portal or the money cannot be paid.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International-track master's and doctoral students in non-clinical, non-contract programmes at the Seoul campus who want a predictable semestral top-up on top of tuition funding or self-funding.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your department sits outside Medicine, Dentistry and Nursing and outside contract-based programmes, and that you are not enrolled at Mirae Campus
Register a bank account in your own name on the Yonsei portal (Academic Information System > Academic Administration > Change Account Information) before the scholarship payment schedule
Protect regular-semester registration - extra or non-regular semesters fall outside the award
Avoid taking a leave of absence or withdrawing mid-semester, which forces full repayment of that semester's disbursement
Check the Graduate School Notice board each semester for scholarship schedule updates
common_rejection_risks: Holding a full Graduate School tuition scholarship for the same regular semesters, which disqualifies you
Enrolment in a clinical college (Medicine, Dentistry, Nursing), a contract-based programme, or Mirae Campus
Studying only in extra/non-regular semesters or pausing study, since support covers regular semesters only
Missing the portal bank-account registration and therefore never receiving a payment
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, admission fees and Seoul living costs are not covered by this stipend - the award is a fixed cash amount per semester and the Graduate School publishes no tuition, housing or travel component.
document_audit: There are no scholarship application documents; the practical paperwork is the personal bank-account registration on the academic portal, and it must be in the student's own name
If a leave of absence or mid-semester withdrawal happens, the full semester disbursement must be returned
alerts: Support stops with regular-semester enrolment: four semesters for master's and doctoral students, six for the integrated programme

Spring 2027 international-track admission ran 7-14 October 2026 with results on 4 December 2026 - entering through that track is what makes the stipend available, but Mirae Campus entrants are excluded
Payment follows the Graduate School scholarship schedule, so the first disbursement can lag registration
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: No scholarship application: admission through the international student track triggers eligibility, and the Graduate School pays the fixed per-semester amount to the bank account registered on the Yonsei portal.
